name: Zed
tagline: A fast, native editor written in Rust
description: A code editor built from scratch for speed, with language servers, a debugger, Git, remote development and real-time collaboration built in rather than added by extensions.
licenseNote: The editor is GPL-3.0, its collaboration server AGPL-3.0 and its UI framework Apache-2.0. Signing in is optional and only needed for collaboration and Zed's hosted AI. Contributions require a contributor licence agreement.
backing: Zed Industries (US, venture-backed), funded by paid AI plans

maturity.rationale: Stable on macOS, Linux and Windows, with weekly releases and a fast-growing extension catalogue. It is younger than VS Code, and some niches are thinner.

strengths: Noticeably faster and lighter than Electron-based editors
Imports VS Code settings and keybindings; Vim and Helix modes are built in
Language servers, a debugger, Git and remote development over SSH are built in
AI features are optional, and work with your own API keys or local models
weaknesses: It cannot run VS Code extensions, and its own catalogue is smaller
Backed by a venture-funded company whose business is AI subscriptions
Some long-tail language and framework tooling is less complete than in VS Code
Collaboration goes through Zed's servers unless you run your own

featureNotes.no-telemetry: On by default; one setting turns it off
